## Wakt 1.0.3

### Website blocking is now DNS-based
- Blocked websites are filtered by a local, DNS-only VPN instead of by reading browser URL bars. Only DNS queries pass through it, so browsing speed and battery are unaffected and nothing leaves your device.
- Because filtering happens at the DNS level, blocking `facebook.com` also stops the Facebook app, and the same for any site whose app uses the same domain.
- The first time you save a website block, Android asks you once to allow the VPN connection.
- Blocked domains get an instant NXDOMAIN answer, other lookups are forwarded to your network's own DNS servers and cached, and temporary unlocks earned through a challenge apply immediately.
- The VPN stops itself when no website blocks remain.
- Known limit: a strict Private DNS setting (DNS over TLS) bypasses the filter.

### Notes
- App blocking, Phone lock, and schedules still use the Accessibility Service, so that permission is still required.
- If Google Play Protect blocks the install, temporarily turn off "Scan apps with Play Protect" in the Play Store, install, then turn it back on.

### Changes since 1.0.2
- 7a8a551 feat: Re-enable website blocking via fast DNS-only VPN
- f799996 ci: Allow releasing from a branch push
- 650e45d build: Only apply release signing config when the keystore exists
